mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the monthly CPIAUCSL inflation index above 2% triggers a preemptive market anticipation of rate hikes, which short-haul suppresses equity valuations and produces negative 20-day S&P 500 forward returns.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL crosses above 2.0 in the current month
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically different from zero during inflation spikes (p > 0.05), or CPIAUCSL remains below 2% for 3 consecutive months without S&P 500 decline.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly rise in PAYEMS labor cost index exceeding 0.5% signals wage pressures that prompt the Federal Reserve to maintain higher rates, reducing equity discount rates and lowering 60-day forward S&P 500 returns.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases by more than 0.5% month-over-month
failure_condition: No significant negative return in 60-day windows following such PAYEMS increases (t-test p > 0.05), or FEDFUNDS declines during the period.

mechanism_narrative: A consecutive monthly increase in HOUST industrial production exceeding 2% suggests strengthening economic demand, which elevates equity risk premia and produces positive 20-day S&P 500 forward returns.
candidate_trigger: HOUST shows 2 consecutive months of >2% growth
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns remain flat or negative despite confirmed demand acceleration (Rank IC < 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp decline in INDPRO supply index below 90 (2017=100 baseline) indicates softening manufacturing capacity, which raises uncertainty and drives negative 20-day S&P 500 forward returns.
failure_condition: No significant negative returns during confirmed supply shocks (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained 3-month decline in FEDFUNDS below 4% creates a risk-off environment where investors discount future cash flows more heavily, producing negative 60-day S&P 500 forward returns.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not statistically negative during such periods (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When UNRATE falls below 4% for two consecutive months, indicating weaker labor market conditions, S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 days tend to be negative due to reduced consumer spending expectations.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE decreases for 2 consecutive months below 4%
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.05) during such UNRATE declines.

mechanism_narrative: Concurrent increases in GDPC1 (demand) and RSAFS (retail) above their 2010-05-15 moving averages by 3% each suggest a strong economic upturn, which drives positive 20-day S&P 500 forward returns.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 and RSAFS both exceed 2010-05-15 moving averages by >3%
failure_condition: No significant positive return in 20 days despite both proxies meeting the threshold (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp drop in GDPC1 demand index below its 2007-09 trough combined with a 10% one-month drop in HOUST production creates a supply shock that produces positive 60-day S&P 500 forward returns as investors price in recovery.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 < 2007-09 trough AND HOUST down 10% in the current month
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns remain flat or negative despite confirmed supply disruption (Rank IC < 0.05).
